name: Human egg cell
headline: diameter
subtitle: Mature oocyte at ovulation
description: The human egg cell, or oocyte, is the female reproductive cell and one of the largest cells in the body. It develops inside a follicle in the ovary and is enclosed by a protective outer coat called the zona pellucida. By ovulation it has reached a final diameter of around 110 to 120 µm, not counting that coat.

measures.label: Diameter at ovulation
measures.note: Final oocyte diameter reached by ovulation, as stated in the paper's introduction

measures.label: Mean measured diameter (mature MII oocytes)
measures.note: 123 +/- 9.7 µm for metaphase II oocytes matured in vitro, measured from the inner side of the zona pellucida (zona not included)

facts.text: In a study of immature human oocytes collected from ovarian tissue and matured in the lab, diameters ranged from 60 to 171 µm, with a mean of 115 µm.
The same study found that oocytes that reached full maturity (metaphase II) were larger on average than those that did not.

sources.publisher: Journal of Assisted Reproduction and Genetics (via PubMed Central, NIH)
sources.title: Oocyte diameter predicts the maturation rate of human immature oocytes collected ex vivo (Pors et al., 2022)

caveats: The study's own measurements exclude the zona pellucida, so the egg with its coat is somewhat wider; no sourced zona thickness was fetched.
Only one source was used; no sourced mass or volume was found.
